solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Eats quickly in barracks

definitions.meaning: to jeer or mock a performer or player, a British sense of the verb

explanation.walkthrough: 'barracks' looks like a noun for soldiers' quarters, but here it is the verb meaning to heckle, joined to the first sense by 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: one gobbles food, and one jeers derisively at someone.

clue.text: Company present books making sense

parts.note: here means present, as in a roll call
NT, the New Testament, is a collection of books

explanation.surface: A company presents books that are logical.
explanation.definitionFit: A coherent argument is logical and intelligible.

clue.text: City left men inside barrier

indicators.note: these two pieces go inside the word for barrier

parts.note: a fence is a barrier
OR, other ranks, is military shorthand for ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: In a city, men are left behind a barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tuscan capital is an Italian city famous for Renaissance art.

clue.text: Poor rodent she cut down

indicators.note: poor suggests the letters of rodent and she are in bad shape and need rearranging

explanation.surface: A pitiable rodent that a woman chopped up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' looks like pity for the rodent, but it signals rearranging RODENT and SHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cut down has been made shorter or abbreviated.

clue.text: Spread left out of enchilada, possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters of the Mexican dish could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A recipe note: this spread has no lettuce leaf in the enchilada, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left out of' tells you to remove L from ENCHILADA; 'possibly' rearranges the remaining letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A spread is an American term for a large ranch or estate, which a Spanish-style estate also is.

clue.text: Trouble with containers, they'll keep you warm

parts.note: being in hot water means being in trouble
bottles are containers

explanation.surface: Trouble with containers, while the containers keep you warm.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubber vessels filled with heated water are placed in beds for warmth.

clue.text: Embrace one person wearing nothing accepting cult, oddly

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: accepting means the word for a naked person takes the letters inside

parts.note: a nude is a person wearing no clothes

indicators.note: oddly picks the odd-numbered letters of cult

explanation.surface: One naked person welcomes a strange cult with open arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes the first and third letters of cult, C and L, which 'accepting' puts inside NUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To embrace something is to take it in as a part of a whole.

clue.text: One tells of Scottish island uprising to leader of rebels

indicators.note: in a down clue uprising means the island name reads upwards

parts.note: Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde, Scotland

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of rebels

explanation.surface: A storyteller recounts a Scottish island's revolt in favour of the rebel chief.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'uprising' reads the island upwards; 'leader of rebels' gives just its first letter, and 'One tells of' is the definition, a person who relates events.
explanation.definitionFit: A storyteller is the person who recounts events in a tale.

clue.text: Adjust picture for broadcast on skirmish

indicators.note: in a down clue, on places the first piece above the second

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
a brush is a brief encounter or skirmish

explanation.surface: Retouching a photo for broadcast of a battle scene.
explanation.definitionFit: To touch up a photograph using a spray device that alters the image.

clue.text: Gunfight that follows penalty?

definitions.meaning: a decisive exchange of fire between gunmen
in football a tied match may be settled by a series of penalty kicks

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading plays on 'penalty' as in the football tie-breaker where players take turns to kick at goal.
explanation.definitionFit: A Wild West showdown between gunslingers bears the same name as football's tie-breaking spot-kick contest.

clue.text: He beats the goalie, giving heart to disheartened star

indicators.note: giving one thing to another puts it into the middle of the other here
the word star loses its central letters, leaving only its ends

parts.note: the core of something is its heart

explanation.surface: A footballer who scores is the star who leaves the opposing keeper dejected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' strips TA from star, leaving S and R; 'giving heart to' puts CORE between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A player who gets the ball past the goalkeeper puts a goal on the board for the team.

clue.text: Inexperienced eleven not finishing drink

parts.note: a novice is called green, as in unripe

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for a side is dropped

parts.note: a cricket or football side of eleven players is a team

explanation.surface: A novice football side that cannot finish the game is having a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an infusion of unfermented tea leaves, a popular beverage.

clue.text: Family help couple to chase gold

indicators.note: chasing means coming after, so this piece follows the other

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a couple is a pair

explanation.surface: A family's helper, paired up, sets off in pursuit of riches.
explanation.definitionFit: A young foreign person living with a family and helping with childcare and housework in return for board.

clue.text: Meet prisoner in front of border

indicators.note: this piece is placed before the next one in the answer

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner
a verge is a grassy border beside a road

explanation.surface: Instructions to meet a released prisoner at the edge of a road.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines or people coming together at one point gather or join up.

clue.text: Apply a coating to good second-hand denture

parts.note: second-hand things are old
a plate is a denture, a set of false teeth

explanation.surface: A dentist gilds a good second-hand set of false teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: To cover a base metal with a thin layer of the precious yellow metal.

clue.text: Small yet volatile infection

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: volatile means unstable, so the letters of yet are rearranged

explanation.surface: A small but unpredictable infection is still a worry.
explanation.definitionFit: A painful swelling on the eyelid caused by a bacterial infection of a gland.

clue.text: Heads off after star gets cover

indicators.note: the rearranged letters follow the word for a star

parts.note: the sun is a star

indicators.note: off suggests the letters of Heads go wrong and are rearranged

explanation.surface: People head off when a star gets cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads off' looks like people departing, but 'off' is the anagram signal working on Heads, and 'after' places that result beneath the star.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasol or awning gives cover from bright light.

clue.text: The old dear loses head, getting a horse

parts.note: ye is an archaic form of the

indicators.note: loses head means the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: darling is a term of affection, dear

explanation.surface: An old lady loses her head over a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: The trimmed word is a synonym: DARLING minus its first letter gives ARLING.
explanation.definitionFit: A yearling is a horse in its second year, between one and two years old.

clue.text: Underhand and underfoot?

definitions.meaning: sly, cunning, knowing in a mischievous way
the curved part of the sole of the foot

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is whimsical: the curved part of the sole is literally under your foot.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is playfully knowing or roguish; the other is the vaulted part of the foot's sole.

clue.text: Investing time in a healthy son causes amazement

indicators.note: investing means putting the abbreviation inside the word for healthy

parts.note: sound means healthy, as in sound mind and body

explanation.surface: Investing time in a healthy son will amaze people.
explanation.definitionFit: To astound someone is to cause them great surprise.

clue.text: Go on do, mostly united in order

parts.note: a do, as a verb, is a swindle or con

indicators.note: in order suggests the letters are put into a new arrangement
mostly means almost all, so the last letter of united is removed

explanation.surface: A party organiser urges everyone to keep going, mostly united in order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims UNITED to UNITE; 'in order' rearranges that to TINUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry on or persist is the same as to keep going.

clue.text: Occasional dances for different people

parts.note: odd can mean occasional, as in the odd visit
balls are formal dances

explanation.surface: Occasional dances attract unusual guests.
explanation.definitionFit: Eccentrics are people who behave strangely, standing out as unconventional.

clue.text: Rich university made advance after work

indicators.note: the remaining pieces come after the abbreviation for work

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
lent means made an advance of money

explanation.surface: A rich university offered a loan after work.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulent means luxuriously wealthy, rich in appearance.

clue.text: New branch organising tours around Portugal

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the abbreviation for the country
organising suggests the letters of tours are put into a fresh order

parts.note: P is the international vehicle registration for Portugal

explanation.surface: A travel company opens a new branch arranging trips around Portugal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organising' rearranges TOURS to SROUT, and 'around' puts P inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoot is a new growth from a plant, a fresh branch.

clue.text: Pastor to supply sources of nourishment

indicators.note: read as supple-ly, flexibly, so the letters of Pastor and to are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A pastor is called upon to provide spiritual nourishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a verb meaning provide, but it is the anagram signal, read as the adverb of supple.
explanation.definitionFit: The main roots of plants draw water and minerals up to feed them.

clue.text: Puts up with second-class, surrounded by assistants

indicators.note: the letter for second-class sits within the word for helpers

parts.note: aides are assistants
B denotes second class, as in a B grade

explanation.surface: Someone tolerates being given second-class treatment while surrounded by helpers.
explanation.definitionFit: To tolerate or bear something is to put up with it.

clue.text: Tendency to absorb right knowledge

indicators.note: the word for a tendency takes in the abbreviation, holding it inside

parts.note: a leaning is an inclination or tendency

explanation.surface: A tendency to absorb the right facts is the mark of a good student.
explanation.definitionFit: Scholarship acquired through study is a body of knowledge.

clue.text: Period that is welcomed by teams rowing

indicators.note: being welcomed by means being taken in by the rowing crews

parts.note: rowing crews of eight oarsmen are called eights
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A period of history when rowing teams were warmly received.
explanation.definitionFit: A decade such as 1980 to 1989 is a period of time.

clue.text: Follows and makes certain, with no resistance

indicators.note: with no indicates that the letter is removed from the word

parts.note: to ensure is to make certain
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Someone follows a plan and makes sure there is no opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that comes after as a result happens next.
